The author tested SenseTime's SenseNova-6.8-Flash across four generation categories—code animation, UI, 3D, and SVG motion posters—and paired it with a self-developed vibecoding-humanizer Skill to remove the AI feel, so you can create dynamic works close to the benchmark with a domestic model. Give it a try!
en.reason: The author runs SenseNova-6.8-Flash on a 15-second code animation and across UI, 3D and SVG poster generation, then reruns it with a self-built vibecoding-humanizer skill, comparing against Opus 5.5 to dissect AI tells in fonts and transitions.

items.title: 评估：如何判断 AI 系统是否真正有效
items.summary: 这篇面向工程师、产品与管理者的分层评估指南，戳破了AI评测里常见的自欺陷阱。作者带大家拆解了代码评分器、模型裁判、幻觉检测器的适用边界，看完你也能搭建一套可落地、可信的评测流水线，用扎实的数据验证每一次迭代，避免分数好看、线上翻车。

items.recommend_reason_zh: 文章以自行车店80张客户支持工单为例，拆解LLM系统评估的输入、系统、评分器和数字流程，并提醒与人类仅60%一致性的评判模型可能掩盖产品问题，评分器本身也必须被测试。

en.title: Evaluation: How to tell if an AI system actually works
en.summary: This layered evaluation guide for engineers, product managers, and managers debunks the common self-deception traps in AI evaluation. The author breaks down where code graders, model judges, and hallucination detectors actually apply, so you can build a practical, trustworthy evaluation pipeline and validate every iteration with solid data—avoiding the trap of great scores and production failures.
en.reason: A bicycle-shop example with 80 customer-support tickets breaks LLM evaluation into inputs, system, graders and scoring, warning that a judge agreeing with humans only 60% of the time can hide product failures and must itself be tested.

DigitalOcean has opened public previews of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling developers to build, evaluate, and continuously optimize AI agents on the same AI-native cloud platform.

Word count: 1,117 words

DigitalOcean has launched public previews of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling AI agents to continuously learn, evaluate, and iteratively improve based on their own data. The services are built on Inference Engine and Managed Agents, creating a "think-execute-improve" loop. The enhanced Inference Router runs independently, supporting dynamic model selection by task and cross-model consistency evaluation.

Insights records agent behavior; Signals automatically identifies failures and performance gaps; Simulations supports realistic conversation simulation testing before deployment.

Suitable for AI engineers, MLOps engineers, and cloud-native platform architects.

en.title: The Evolution of Agent Harness: From Chains and Graphs to Code
en.summary:
Agent systems built on large models have moved from linear prompts to graph-based workflows and, more recently, to Harness — executable code. This article recommends validating model outputs and choosing the simplest approach that meets reliability, speed, and cost requirements.

4,596 words · about a 15-minute read

LLM agents are evolving from simple prompt chaining into structured execution frameworks (Harness) with observability and stability. Business needs are driving the shift, which has moved through three paradigms: chaining, tool augmentation, and structured control. LinkedIn's early work used LangChain to build a three-step route–retrieve–generate chain, treating the LLM as a black-box text function.

The chaining paradigm is essentially linear prompt orchestration: fast to ship but hard to control; separating routing from retrieval reflects a task-decoupling design; the core value of the Harness framework is a deterministic execution scaffold for probabilistic models.

Intended for AI engineering leads, LLM application architects, and agent platform developers.

Over the past few years, agents built on large language models have changed dramatically. At first they were just glue code cobbled together
en.reason: Large language model agents have moved from linear prompt chains through graph-based workflows to executable-code Harness frameworks, illustrated by LinkedIn’s early LangChain three-step routing, retrieval and generation chain, with the article urging output validation and the simplest option that meets reliability, speed and cost needs.

DigitalOcean has opened public previews of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling developers to build, evaluate, and continuously optimize AI agents on the same AI-native cloud platform.

Word count: 1,117 words
Estimated reading time: about 4 minutes

DigitalOcean has launched public previews of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling AI agents to continuously learn, evaluate, and iteratively improve based on their own data. The services are built on Inference Engine and Managed Agents, creating a "think-execute-improve" loop. The enhanced Inference Router runs independently, supporting dynamic model selection by task and cross-model consistency evaluation.

Insights records agent behavior; Signals automatically identifies failures and performance gaps; Simulations supports realistic conversation simulation testing before deployment.

Suitable for AI engineers, MLOps engineers, and cloud-native platform architects.
en.reason: DigitalOcean opened public previews of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, letting AI agents learn from their own data and iterate through Insights, Signals and Simulations, which test conversations before deployment and fix issues before a 400th user hits them.

en.title: The Evolution of Agent Harness: From Chains and Graphs to Code
en.summary:
Agent systems built on large models have moved from linear prompts to graph-based workflows and, more recently, to Harness — executable code. This article recommends validating model outputs and choosing the simplest approach that meets reliability, speed, and cost requirements.

4,596 words · about a 15-minute read

LLM agents are evolving from simple prompt chaining into structured execution frameworks (Harness) with observability and stability. Business needs are driving the shift, which has moved through three paradigms: chaining, tool augmentation, and structured control. LinkedIn's early work used LangChain to build a three-step route–retrieve–generate chain, treating the LLM as a black-box text function.

The chaining paradigm is essentially linear prompt orchestration: fast to ship but hard to control; separating routing from retrieval reflects a task-decoupling design; the core value of the Harness framework is a deterministic execution scaffold for probabilistic models.

Intended for AI engineering leads, LLM application architects, and agent platform developers.

en.reason: Large language model agents have moved from linear prompt chains through graph-based workflows to executable-code Harness frameworks, illustrated by LinkedIn’s early LangChain three-step routing, retrieval and generation chain, with the article urging output validation and the simplest option that meets reliability, speed and cost needs.
